In mathematics, the '''Barban–Davenport–Halberstam theorem''' is a statement about the distribution of [[prime number]]s in an [[arithmetic progression]].  It is known that in the long run primes are distributed equally across possible progressions with the same difference.  Theorems of the Barban–Davenport–Halberstam type give estimates for the error term, determining how close to [[Uniform distribution (discrete)|uniform]] the distributions are.

==Statement==
Let ''a'' be [[coprime integers|coprime]] to ''q'' and

:<math>\vartheta(x;q,a) = \sum_{p\leq x \,;\, p \equiv a \bmod q} \log p \  </math>

be a weighted count of primes in the arithmetic progression ''a''&nbsp;mod&nbsp;''q''.  We have

:<math>\vartheta(x;q,a) = \frac{x}{\varphi(q)} + E(x;q,a) \ </math>

where ''&phi;'' is [[Euler's totient function]] and the error term ''E'' is small compared to&nbsp;''x''.  We take a sum of squares of error terms

:<math>V(x,Q) = \sum_{q \leq Q} \sum_{a \bmod{q}} |E(x;q,a)|^2 \ . </math>

Then we have

:<math>V(x,Q) = O(Q x \log x) + O(x^2 (\log x)^{-A}) \ </math>

for <math>1 \leq Q  \leq x </math> and  every positive&nbsp;''A'', where ''O'' is [[Big O notation|Landau's Big O notation]].

This form of the theorem is due to Gallagher.  The result of Barban is valid only for <math>Q \leq x (\log x)^{-B}</math> for some ''B'' depending on ''A'', and the result of Davenport–Halberstam has&nbsp;''B''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''A''&nbsp;+&nbsp;5.
